correctness.rationale: Real Walsh characters diagonalize the cube Laplacian at 2j with multiplicity binom(n,j). PBH is exactly injectivity of each eigenspace restriction. For n=2r+1, the adjoint inclusion and deletion operators obey DU−UD=(n−2k)I at rank k; raising is injective below the middle. At rank t the primitive kernel is spanned by disjoint pair differences: choose each ballot top set b1<…<bt with bi≥2i, greedily match disjoint non-tops ai<bi, and use the top sets as distinct leading monomials of the kernel products. The ballot count is binom(n,t)−binom(n,t−1), the primitive dimension. Adjointness gives the orthogonal decomposition of their raised images. Each chosen pair straddling X contributes −2 times its pair difference, and any nonstraddling pair cancels. The remaining coefficient of z^(j−t) in (1−z²)^(r−t)(1+z) is the nonzero signed binomial in the proof. Thus each primitive sector maps isomorphically to its corresponding target sector for j≤r. Frequency complements give all higher ranks and vertex complements give the other actuator layer. In even dimension the central restriction has proportional complementary columns, and all other layer sizes are below the largest multiplicity. Independently computed ranks modulo 101 for all fixed levels at n=3,5,7,9 equal their full column counts; this certifies these finite ranks over R, not the general theorem.
residual_risks: The proof is about real exact controllability and independent input columns for the uniform undirected cube; it does not extend to general weighted networks or constrained inputs.
